articles.title: The Telekinetic Phenomena of Lamia 1929
articles.excerpt: Report on the telekinetic phenomena and psychic investigation in Lamia, led by Angelos Tanagras.

content.value: Much was said recently about the telekinetic phenomena in Lamia, where about a year ago stones began falling on hotelier Stoukas' house, causing panic. To get a reliable opinion we turned to Angelos Tanagras, the only Greek specialist in Psychic Research, who told us the following:

Well, said Mr. Tanagras, some people, when they hear something beyond what they know, shrug and smile as if they have solved all the problems of the universe. One of them forty years ago laughed at the phonograph, calling believers fools. Yet they themselves accept far more astonishing things: that Earth is a round sphere with fiery liquid inside its crust (as volcanoes prove), that right now we are hurtling at 370 km per second toward Capricornus, and much more.

But when they hear of telepathy or telekinesis they look at you with a silly pitying grin. They are like flocks following the shepherd; once the servant and the greengrocer are convinced, they will follow too without realizing it. Most people are like that-fortunately not everyone.
The Lamia phenomena
We asked him to describe the Lamia events. (On his desk among photos and ornaments sat a small ash-colored stone inscribed 'Telekinetic Phenomena of Lamia,' which we asked about.)

Ah yes! he said. It is one of the stones that fell for about a year on Stoukas' house in Lamia. Although such a phenomenon-easy to fake and defraud-is normally disregarded in research, I could not resist taking one for the Psychic Research Museum.

These stones, despite their sometimes considerable weight, caused no harm even when they struck people. A policeman was hit in the stomach and barely felt it. Another, about 1.5 kg, rested on the vines, and a third did not even crack the entry tile when it fell-as if the stones lost their weight. The same effect was recently noted in Czechoslovakia by neurologist Simsa and teacher Vratnik, who studied it in detail with medium Hilda.
Stone-throwing by invisible hands
How long did it last?

A full year with small breaks. The entire Lamia police mobilized to see if it was a malicious attack but found nothing. Imagine the indignation of good Stoukas when neighbors deemed him damned and his home demonic. He decided to leave for his village Kastania.
In vain-the stone-throwing followed him there and returned with him to Lamia in October. Then the phenomena abruptly changed form: the stones stopped and objects began to move.
Machines that walk
First a sewing machine began strolling through the rooms. Then its wooden case did the same.
How is that explained?
Just as a magnet draws iron. It is a simple natural phenomenon.
Where does it come from?
From the same cause as the stone-throwing: someone in the family. As we later confirmed, it was the 13-year-old maid Maria Hani.
Could the girl have produced the phenomena on purpose?
We suspected that at first, but soon realized the stones fell even when Maria was in her room, and the object movements occurred when she was away from the house.
What impression did the movements make?
The family panicked and resorted to religion. The Metropolitan, knowing it was a natural phenomenon, stayed out of it. But Father Spyros Styraatoulos, boasting power over Satan, performed a blessing.
The result: icons, oil lamps, and censers shot from the shrine; Father Spyros fled to a cafe for water to recover his nerves.
Since then objects have not stopped flying. The story spread and crowds came to watch.
Did many witness it?
Who verified it

Crowds of Lamia residents: doctor Mousatos, whose armchair with wooden arms broke before him; Lt. Colonel Kolias; Major Bountouris; Major Gardikis-all observed the phenomena, with sworn statements in the January issue of Psychikai Ereynai.

The funniest was seminary student Chasiakos, who thought it was a hoax. He sat on a chair by the door; suddenly a liter bottle of olive oil 'paid him a visit,' smashing on his seat, drenching him and nicking his neck. He gathered his cassock and ran shouting it was Satan's work.

Then the lit brazier overturned, chairs fell, life in the house became unbearable-even though the hosts, seeing no real damage done, quickly regained courage in their Roumeliote way. Often when an object moved they set it back like a naughty child saying, 'You'll stay there now!'-only for it to fly off again.
The strangest event was moving a 10-month-old baby, the child of tenant Spiridoula Ketiaki. The swaddled infant was shifted three meters from its cradle while sleeping. The mother rushed to grab it.

As neighbors discussed it, a chair fell; before they recovered, a roughly 40-kg table with metal legs began moving on its own. Everyone bolted outside in terror while Spiridoula, holding the baby, begged her husband to leave the house.
How the phenomena are explained
What is their significance?

Immense from a human viewpoint. These phenomena are not aimless like a magnet pulling iron; they prove a conscious force carries them out. That conscious force is emitted from a human body. What shall we call it? Humans always called it 'soul.' Telekinesis is living proof of the soul's existence-a long-sought proof that will persuade the world and give humanity a new mentality.
Have you seen telekinesis yourself?
Yes, in Heraklion, Crete, together with the most skeptical scientists there-doctors Vogiatzakis and Markatatos-whom I invited, fearing hallucination.

Telekinesis exists; it is a fact, as is the existence of soul. That few have seen or believed it means nothing: a phenomenon proven experimentally never disappears. Tomorrow will vindicate those who introduced scientific research on psychic matters to Greece, even if they seek no triumphs.
Empros newspaper - 11 January 1929
Following the previous GSPR communique about 13-year-old medium Maria Hani: the object movements stopped and the medium began having hallucinations.
She thought she saw in the yard a short robed figure-imagined as a saint-ordering her to tell the Stoukas family to leave the house by St. Andrew's eve or suffer great harm.
Terrified, the family followed the GSPR's advice and sent the girl back to her village.
Since then nothing happened-neither on the date she named nor afterwards.
The GSPR will monitor the young medium's development and, if needed, bring her to its offices.

articles.title: An Entire Army of Vampires — Appearing Every Year in Crete
articles.author: Angelos Tanagras
articles.excerpt: Eyewitness accounts of the annual apparition of General Chatzimichalis' slaughtered army at Frangokastello in Crete, with a scientific analysis by the president of the Society for Psychical Research.

content.value: Eyewitness accounts: all the vrykolakes leap with their horses, circle the castle, and vanish. Maria Pliakaki surpasses even the Abbot of Agios Charalambos in tragic detail. On the failure of the British Society for Psychical Research — The tangible vision.

Athens. Before proceeding to the illuminating interview with the distinguished president of the Society for Psychical Research, it is necessary to describe to our readers the landscape in which the vision of General Chatzimichalis' army — slaughtered many years ago — appears. The Venetian castle
According to the supplementary account of Mr. Tanagras, the phenomenon appears shortly before sunrise while a light breeze is blowing.
Readers should retain these details carefully in their memory. They will help them understand the scientific explanation — as conceived by Mr. Tanagras — of the phenomenon.
Some Testimonies:
Let us now hear some accounts from eyewitnesses.
The Abbot of the nearby monastery of Agios Charalambos, Charalambis — or Hatzipateras as his fellow villagers call him — recounted the following to Mr. Tanagras' associates:
— For years now each May I see this thing in the sky. God have mercy on us. My grandfather told me these are the souls of the dead slaughtered by the Turks, who are seeking rest.
— What, grandfather, I asked, must be done for them to be laid in their graves?
And his grandfather replied:
— We must bring their bones out from the mountain and the sea and bury them in consecrated ground, blessed by a priest, so that their spirits may find peace.
— Very well, they ask him, what do you see?
Hatzipateras, polishing his boots, recounts:

— What can I tell you, I get dizzy just thinking about it. You'd say it was night and I was seeing it in my sleep. I see it wide awake and it startles me. There, before the sun is half a metre high, a haziness takes hold of the sky. And the sun, half risen, is the colour of blood. And then, clouds leap about opposite...
— And then?
— There they all leap together with their horses and circle the castle before vanishing.
— Can you see faces clearly, Hatzipateras?
— Good heavens, of course I can. Their noses, their feet, their palms, their rifles — all perfectly clear.

And you know another thing — when the villagers and the women and children make the sign of the cross and call on the Virgin and the Cross for help, they vanish and do not reappear. And they vanish and reappear and make 13 circuits around Frangokastello, then vanish. It is as if the north wind takes them and sends them back...
The Women's Imagination
The women's accounts are more tragic. Maria Pliakaki recounts:

— Ten years now I have been seeing 'The Greeks.' I was at Charakas (a village in Messara) when I first saw them. I was at the village well one morning to fetch water, together with other girls. The sun had not yet risen and as an old woman, Kyratsas Christaina, was pulling up the bucket, she let out a great cry.

— My God, Holy Mother, there are the vrykolakes! she cried, and pointed to the sky. We all looked up and saw the vrykolakes, black against red clouds, marching frantically. They brandished their swords and struck out in our direction. Three girls fainted from fright.
We went and placed incense at our windows and the vrykolakes went back to their graves.
A younger Cretan woman present, a well-nourished girl, observes:

— What graves, you fool? They have no graves — that is why they haunt us every year. I heard their voices myself, and the voice of the nun who was gathering the bones of the dead. I also saw the Devil fleeing from them the year before last. It is because the holy Nun is chasing him...
The Scientific Ambush

Now that our readers have a full picture both of the villagers' imaginings and of the appearance of the vision as described yesterday, let us give the floor to the learned and esteemed president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Tanagras. He received us at his home, where the Society's offices are also located...

Piles of books here, suits of armour there, glass-headed Chinese figures mocking the skeleton of a wild animal, a skull beside the inkwell. Photographs of mediums and portraits of international figures in psychiatry and of psychical research societies from around the world.
With his characteristic gentleness he tells us:

— The phenomenon of Sfakia in Crete was brought to our attention through accounts and letters from there. Unfortunately we lacked the funds to undertake a journey all the way to Sfakia. Society unfortunately does not give the importance it should to the work of our Society.

— We were faced with the fact that last year the British Society for Psychical Research sent an expedition consisting of Messrs. Bennett and White to Crete to ascertain what was happening. I can inform you that the world press covered the phenomenon, and spiritualists claimed it was proof of...
It was precisely for that verification that we decided this year to go to Sfakia as well. It would have been a shame for foreigners to be investigating a phenomenon from our own land.
— What did the British expedition establish, Mr. Tanagras?

— Nothing. That is not their fault, of course — men of the calibre of Bennett and White are beyond reproach. The weather was unfavourable and the vision did not appear. They waited for several days and, finding nothing, departed. But no sooner had they left than the army of the so-called 'Greeks' appeared...
— Were you luckier than them, Mr. President?

— I shall tell you at once. The British expedition's visit and its failure were one more reason that pushed us to go to Crete. The phenomenon, according to the information we had, appears each year at the end of May by the new calendar — around 15–17 May by the old calendar — the date coinciding with...

We had four cameras with us, lent to us by Mrs. Choremi. We set them up in the right position and waited. Only photographing the vision would resolve the matter. It was a case of collective suggestion, but the cause of the vision that all of Crete claims to have seen with their own eyes was something else entirely...
— What is your impression, Mr. Tanagras?
— That the phenomenon most certainly occurs.

articles.title: 'Haunted Houses' - GSPR Investigations of Their Phenomena
articles.excerpt: Angelos Tanagras' lecture on haunted houses in Mavrovo and Kozani: detailed accounts of telekinetic outbreaks, the medium Kalliopi, and the call for a research institute.

content.value: Astonishing things confirmed in Macedonia
Yesterday’s Lecture
As had been announced, Mr Angelos Tanagras gave his lecture yesterday afternoon in the hall of the Academy, on “the phenomena of haunted houses” at Mavrovo and at Kozani.

The hall was packed to suffocation with men of science and representatives of every social class. The ladies were in the majority, and among the clergy the Metropolitans of Corfu and of Arta were to be seen.

Mr Tanagras began by recounting how he had travelled to Mavrovo and to Kozani in order to study the phenomena of the haunted houses that had been written about. The mission was a delicate and difficult one, and it appeared besides that what was involved was telekinesis. For this reason, he said, he had been sceptical about the incidents, and had in mind similar examples reported by Lombroso, Flammarion and others.
The history of haunted houses

He then examined what “haunted houses” mean in science. All over the world and in every age, haunted houses have appeared exactly as we too understand them. In antiquity it is recorded that Pausanias, when he had been accused of treason, took refuge in the temple of Athena Chalkioikos. From that time the temple ceased to be used, because every evening lamentations, groans and other strange and terrifying noises were heard. Pliny, describing these occurrences of haunted houses, advised the Athenians to avoid them. The sceptical philosopher Athenodoros, however, scorning this advice, asked to live in such a house, but quickly changed his mind, for he heard knockings, and the ghost of an old man appeared before him and made a sign for him to follow it out into the garden, where it vanished. When he reported these phenomena to the local authorities, a search was made in the garden and a human skeleton was found bound in chains.

There are countless similar occurrences in the history and the traditions of peoples. In earlier ages these were attributed to demonic possession, and superstition, combined with scientific ignorance, made those who experienced them appear in the eyes of other men as possessed.

In recent years, by the light of science, these phenomena have been distinguished and given a solution, an explanation, while observations and investigations continue. The finding of suitable “mediums” is rare, and Eusapia Palladino is cited from years ago. But the phenomenon of Kalliopi of Kozani was unprecedented. Palladino would not have come near her little finger, had this medium been trained properly and not been left to go to ruin — for unfortunately such knowledge was not then widespread.
He goes on to describe his journey to Kastoria, where he met some well-qualified men of science who were following these matters scientifically and with great diligence.

Mr Tanagras met with the investigating committee, made up of local scientists and officials, in the village of Mavrovo, where various telekinetic phenomena had been reported in the house of Mr Mavromatis, an old chieftain.
It was reported that astonishing things were happening. Apparitions presented themselves, stones fell, the house was “possessed”, and so forth.
That these were hoaxes was ruled out at once, because the host was not a man who would permit such contrivances; besides, the phenomena themselves refute any such suspicion.

The Mavromatis household consisted of the husband, the wife, the children and a young servant girl. That the stone-throwing was aimed at the family is out of the question, because the damage was extensive and fell upon household objects and utensils. Nothing was left in its place. Nor could the surrounding inhabitants have caused it. The house stood in an isolated position and one could see all around it from outside. The imitation of such events is likewise ruled out. Moreover an eyewitness, Papanikolas of the village, while reading a blessing in the house, saw a warm stone fall in the corridor, when it was impossible for it to have landed there had anyone thrown it from any direction whatever. The stone was warm because it had been under the influence of the sun; and the stones fell from eight in the evening until sunset, and all of them were warm.
The first phenomena

When Mr Tanagras heard all this, he recalled similar descriptions by Lombroso, Flammarion and others, who characterise these phenomena by knocks small or large upon glass, by knocks on wood and iron, movements of furniture, the opening of doors (as happened also at the house of Professor Mr Gkizis), the stripping of beds, the extinguishing of candles, the falling of pictures, the illusion of fire, the levitation of chairs, the movement of clocks that had stood stopped for years, and so on.
It was before phenomena of this kind that he found himself at Mavrovo as well, and for that reason he proceeded to a careful examination while maintaining his scepticism.

Once the family were satisfied of the phenomena, they began to look for an explanation, and the first thing they did was to speak of diabolical workings on the part of the servant girl, who had been taken into service as a small child. But of course there was no proof. At first, the loss of small things was noticed in the house — pins, rags — which then appeared inexplicably in the garden.
They supposed that spells were being cast, and further misunderstandings arose, such as that the objects were being stolen by the neighbours.

These first occurrences, however, soon began to take on a larger form. The damage grew more serious, and the head of the family took harsher measures, so that what was happening should not appear a joke, either inside his house or outside it.

Everything was breaking — window panes, glassware; everything was being torn — the clothes, the ties, the raincoats, the mattresses, the caps, all in the same manner and by preference the new ones. They began with a triangular tear and then were torn right through. Of all the glassware, the only thing that survived was a single tumbler.
Everything… flies and is overturned

In the course of the year in which these events were taking place, the destruction spread to the foodstuffs as well. Barrels of cheese fell over, the paraffin and the milk were spilled, the flour flew out of the storeroom sprinkled with water. All the food in the storeroom was scattered, to the point of a desperate state of affairs. The family left the house, because they could no longer either feed themselves or cook, since the pots fell or were hurled about.
The inhabitants of the district, malicious and wary at first, would go to see the “haunted house”, or the “devil’s house”, as they called it.

For six months the phenomena were slight, but afterwards, for thirteen days running, they developed great intensity. The eyewitness Dr Stanos, ruling out the servant girl, became a witness himself of the phenomena of the hurling of the flour, the overturning of furniture and the rest. The former deputy Mr Tsantilis and the student Mr Papalamprou witnessed similar incidents.
On one occasion the whole family except seven-year-old Panagiota was away from the house, and Panagiota suddenly saw things being flung about all over it.

On another occasion a large table came down from the upper floor to the lower. Another time, the owner saw a stone break the window pane, a stone which it was impossible should have been thrown from outside. Another time, a large round table rolled about on the floor together with frying pans and the like. The tables and the chairs danced.
What is the explanation

Mr Tanagras spoke of the explanation of these phenomena and fell back upon the acceptance of telepathy and of hypnosis, which science admits, just as it admits the transmission of a sound by wireless.

What comes first is always the phenomenon of the dynamism our body possesses. It is possible for this force to act contrary to the known rules of mechanics. The chief cause of these phenomena is always a person living in the “haunted houses”, and is termed the “dynamogenic” or “dynamolytic” cause — always involuntary and unconscious, as radium draws upon atomic dynamism.
What the medium is like

He goes on to describe the steps he took at Kastoria and at Kozani towards founding a centre of the Society, and his visit to the medium, the aforementioned Kalliopi, married in a village in Grevena, thirty-five years of age.

This woman was thin, with wild and very strange eyes. At fifteen she suffered meningitis, and after her treatment she had heavy sweating and pains in the stomach. These phenomena are of great medical value, according to Mr Tanagras.

She would see the dance of the furniture before her. When she looked at one of the pieces, it fell to the floor. Above all, she could not stomach the Turks, because they had tried to convert her to Islam.

It was observed that she herself felt a weight equal to the weight of the object being moved. Wherever she passed, everything was overturned or fell. The tables spun round to right and to left. The objects in the rooms passed through windows fitted with bars, while it was observed that if the windows had panes of glass, the objects did not pass.
At other times she would see plates flying through the air, and when they fell they did not break. When, however, other people were present in the room, the objects broke as they fell.

The same happened with sacks of wheat at Mrs Chalkia’s. Her servant said, “Rather than we should wear ourselves out, why not tell Kalliopi…” — and indeed they rolled by themselves into the storeroom, all but the last one, as the servant observed.

Once, a squirrel skin stuffed with straw went hopping about the house, and the plates and forks hung in the air. And another time, an icon followed her, floating, out of the house, although they had tied it down so that it should not move.

So many other phenomena besides that it is impossible to relate them — which, however, gradually ceased when Kalliopi married. At the beginning, one day, her dowry was found hung up on nails, and her mother-in-law was enraged. She said she had put them there, excusing herself, so that the moths should not eat them…
Later her husband abandoned her and went to America. After seven years she married a shepherd in the village of Miloneti, but he too walked out on her and left her with two children.

Mr Tanagras hypnotised her and persuaded her to come here to Athens. The local people undertook to maintain her two children, and she was admitted to the hospital at Kozani in order to reproduce the phenomena under scientific conditions with the doctors there.
The conclusion

And Mr Tanagras concluded that if certain old memories return to her, we shall gain a medium of the greatest value, one that will do honour to Greek science. He also stressed the need to found an Institute, as was done in France through the bequest of the private individual Jean Meyer. For, he says, this science will lead us to the knowledge of the purpose of life. Until now we see only these phenomena and remain ignorant of the cause. We shall come to know our exact destination.
We shall learn that we are temporary inhabitants of this ephemeral planet, and that we shall fly off to other azure expanses when we come to our rest. For the pains of life? Let us hope so…

articles.title: Telekinetic Activity 1925 - Crete
articles.excerpt: Two dream warnings foretold a grandfather's death in Neapoli, Crete-an example of symbolic and vivid telepathic impressions.

content.value: Professor Spyridon K. Georgiou, appointed in 1925 to the Neapoli Gymnasium of Crete, was living there with his mother when one Friday morning she awoke deeply upset by a dream.
She had seen many deceased relatives, dressed for a celebration, going to her father's house-50 km away-for some official occasion.
She interpreted the dream as certain proof of her father's death. Georgiou tried to reassure her, stressing they would have been notified if something bad had happened.
The next night a second dream increased her agitation and certainty: she saw her father all dressed up, taking her hand, kissing her, and saying, 'I'm leaving, my child...'
This time nothing could calm her: 'Say what you like...I am sure father is dead.'
Georgiou, himself influenced by the dreams, withdrew to his room and noted the dates.

Three days later a letter from his uncle announced the grandfather's death on Saturday night-the night of the second dream-and added that the dying man kept asking for his daughter whom he loved dearly.
Here we have two telepathic experiences corresponding to the two dreams: the first symbolic, the second representational.
In the first, Mrs. Georgiou's Subconscious (or soul) sensed telepathically-perhaps from the physicians attending the dying man-his hopeless condition and imminent end.
The impression could also have come from the old man's own anxious thoughts. Her brain symbolized the impression as a dream of dead relatives coming to receive the soon-to-die.
There is a widespread belief that deceased relatives appear at the moment of death to welcome their own.

articles.title: Long Distance Psychic Phenomena
articles.excerpt: Examples of dramatic telepathic impressions at the moment of death-from a dying mother's message to a guitar's sudden vibration-and what they imply about the soul.

content.value: The vision is representational telepathy with an auditory illusion, because those words were not actually spoken. Telepathy gave Mr. Rouben the impression of hearing the dying woman's thought.

It is also possible that the telepathic impression of death automatically triggered Mr. Rouben's own thoughts about protecting his sisters-thoughts he already had after the doctor warned of his mother's desperate condition.

Another case: Shortly before the death of Nikolaos Koutsogiannis, director of the legal department of the National Bank, his doctor Georgios Moschidis escorted the dying man's sister, Mrs. Maria Moschou, home so she would not be present at the death.
As they sat on a sofa waiting for coffee, suddenly-before fifteen minutes had passed-they heard a guitar hanging on the wall opposite, about two meters high, vibrate loudly.
It was a strong 'grrring' as if all the strings had quivered at once. Frightened, they looked at each other and said the dying man must have just passed; they immediately checked the time.
Indeed, at that exact moment the patient expired. He loved to play the guitar, often accompanied in song by Mr. Moschidis, his close friend.
This episode and another described in the previous issue of Astynomika Chronika (at Prof. Varth. Gyzi's home) are characteristic examples of this striking form of deathbed telepathy.

Two explanations are possible. First: the dying man, through his beloved instrument, wanted to signal his sister and friend. This is the simplest, most seemingly logical, and most satisfying to human mysticism.

Second: one of the two mourners-perhaps Mrs. Moschou, who has strong intuition-was the unconscious cause. She subconsciously sensed her brother's death, but her Subconscious, for unknown reasons, could not send the impression to the brain in one of the usual forms (vision, image, psychopathic reaction, etc.).

Faced with that difficulty, it emitted a dynamolytic wave-a kind of psychic discharge-that vibrated the guitar strings symbolically so they would understand the calamity. Folk experience, which never errs in such cases, treats such manifestations as indisputable signs.
This dynamolytic wave-a sort of human 'radioactivity'-does not act like a blind force (a lightning bolt overturning an object) but like a rational will with a specific aim.

Thus, despite materialist dogmas, in critical moments certain people's bodies emit an unknown dynamic factor invisible to the senses which, though lacking flesh, muscle, bone, or brain, acts as if it possessed them.
In other words, we reach confirmation of the term Soul.

Because telekinetic phenomena can be proven experimentally, humanity today stands before an experimental proof of one of life's greatest problems-the soul-that philosophy tried to solve for thousands of years.

If this second explanation does not satisfy humanity's longing to communicate with beloved dead, it at least proves another great hope humanity has always intuited: that not everything about us is mere matter and blind mechanics; we are not just products of blind laws and chance.
Something spiritual, immaterial, immortal, and incorruptible exists within us which-in certain moments-can act consciously outside the body, wielding superhuman powers.

articles.excerpt: A nightingale's farewell song appears in its owner's dream the night it dies-an example of telepathy or clairvoyant sensing between humans and animals.

content.value: The 1925 volume of Psychikai Ereynai published a strange telepathy episode about birds that could also be clairvoyance.

Maria Velissariou had a nightingale from Syria, where these birds are bred. She loved it so much she tended it herself, but when she fell gravely ill with typhoid others cared for it, which left her anxious.
During her recovery she dreamed one night that the nightingale flew to her shoulder and sang sweeter than ever, enchanting her.
In the morning she told her husband, who laughed that she saw her beloved bird even in sleep.
Soon after, to their surprise, the cook announced the nightingale was found dead in its cage.
Perhaps her Subconscious-freed during sleep and weakened by typhoid-sensed the bird's death and symbolized it as a farewell song.
With that explanation there is no need for telepathy between bird and sleeper.
Yet telepathy episodes between humans and animals are so convincing that the phenomenon can be considered indisputable.

articles.title: Telepathy Case of Christovasilis and His Horse
articles.excerpt: Christovasilis' mare refused to continue and likely saved him from brigands; later he saw a black cross just as he learned his son had died-symbolic telepathy in both episodes.

content.value: As a continuation of the cases of telepathy between man and animal, we set down the following: the father of the writer Christovasilis was a tax farmer of the tithe in Asia Minor, and had set out on horseback for a certain village.
On the way, his mare suddenly refused to go on. In vain he tried to force her with persistent spurring. The animal reared up, but would not take a single step.
Faced with this inexplicable “strike” on the part of his mount, he was obliged, against his will, to return to the place from which he had set out, and to recount the animal’s strange obstinacy.
— “You did well!” the villagers then approved, as an echo of popular experience. “The horse knew something. Something bad would have happened to you.”
And indeed, the next day it became known that a caravan coming from the opposite direction had been attacked by bandits, who killed and wounded many and plundered the merchandise as well.
This episode, like that of Sarandidis — also in Asia Minor — constitutes indisputable proof of the possibility of telepathy between man and animal.

Christovasilis’s mare sensed telepathically the impending murderous affray. And because her Subconscious could not transmit the news clearly to the reason, it produced in the animal that characteristic terror and the refusal to continue on towards the dangerous direction.

On another occasion Christovasilis himself, on the Monday of Carnival, went in the morning to his office. There he was astonished, because he kept seeing, persistently and vividly, a black cross on the wall opposite.
He had not yet sat down when they came to call him from his house. There he found many of his close friends, who had come to announce to him the death of his son in Athens.
In this case it is a matter of telepathy of the symbolic kind. Someone who knew the news transmitted it unconsciously to Christovasilis’s Subconscious.
The latter, unable to pass it on clearly to the brain, produced a visual hallucination which symbolised the misfortune by the black cross.

articles.title: The Case of Doctor Ignatios Papakonstantinidis - 1902 & 1914
articles.excerpt: Dreams guided Dr. Papakonstantinidis to ace unexpected exam topics in Constantinople (1902) and warned of an attempted stabbing in Philadelphia, Asia Minor (1914).

content.value: After graduating from the University of Athens in June 1902, Dr. Ignatios Papakonstantinidis went to Constantinople to sit exams to practice medicine there. Exams were only in French or Turkish, which most candidates did not know.

He applied and was scheduled for July 20. Four or five days before, he dreamt he would be examined in French by only two professors: Anatomy on the kidneys and Obstetrics on eclampsia-and that he would pass. It seemed impossible because the obstetrics professor was not on the board.

Still, he studied the kidneys from a French textbook and skimmed eclampsia. On exam day only the Surgery and Anatomy professors appeared; instead of the Ophthalmology professor, the Obstetrics professor came (the former had left for a congress in Brussels).

The dream came true: he was examined first and answered perfectly. The other 12 candidates failed because they had not prepared Obstetrics. With keen intuition he had telepathically sensed the change in examiners.

He also reported to the GSPR another telepathy case: on the night of 22 February 1914 in Philadelphia, Asia Minor, his wife woke frightened from a dream of two disguised Turks knocking; he went to see who it was while she tried to stop him.

Five days later two disguised Turks actually knocked; because the maid was asleep, he opened, and they stabbed him in the chest. His shout made them think he was dead and they fled. The knife struck a pin on his cravat, slipped, and only grazed him.

The next day a Turkish friend warned him to leave for safety. The first part of the dream was pure telepathy: his wife received the decision of the would-be attackers. His survival can be explained by their intent merely to intimidate, the lucky deflection on the pin, or possibly telepathic suggestion causing the assassin's hand to veer.

articles.title: Intuitive and Dynamolytic Faculties - Mrs. Fragkidou's Telepathy
articles.excerpt: Mrs. Eleni K. Fragkidou reported a night of relentless knocks across rooms the exact hour her uncle died-an example of strong intuitive and dynamolytic abilities.

content.value: Mrs. Eleni K. Fragkidou submitted the following to the GSPR:
'As a young girl in Leonidio, my aunt was urgently called to Piraeus, where her only brother was in danger. My cousin stayed alone at home and begged me to sleep beside her.

Around 7 p.m., while in the dining room, I heard loud crashes-as if many glass pieces broke together-inside the sideboard. I called my cousin from the next room to open it; everything was in perfect order.
Soon even stronger, continuous bangs terrified us so much that we fled to a small room hoping for peace. The bangs followed us there.

We moved a third time; again the knocks pursued us with the same intensity. They continued without pause from 9 p.m. until morning, when a telegram arrived: death had occurred precisely at 9 p.m.-the moment the knocks began.'
Mrs. Fragkidou is gifted with powerful intuitive and dynamolytic faculties, as seen in other incidents in her life.

It is therefore closer to the truth to attribute the knocks to her. The telepathic impression of her uncle's death, received by her Subconscious instead of a vision or a mood (representational or psychopathic telepathy), caused an emission of dynamolyte-part of her psychodynamic force.

To signal the misfortune, this force vibrated the air to imitate the knocks. The persistence shows purpose: the Subconscious wanted all night to make the two cousins grasp that the fateful event had occurred.

Because of unknown conditions it could not choose a clearer manifestation. Here the kinship of electricity and psychic emission is obvious: electricity also has preferred conduits; lightning shows curious choices.

Electricity, electromagnetism, X and gamma rays, ultraviolet and infrared are forms of the creative energy that constitutes the universe-intermediate states between spirit and matter. In all bodies, material or semi-material, the same creative power underlies everything.

We are little gods whose superhuman faculties are stifled by material condensation. One day, when the energy we are returns through death to its source-whether or not it retained life's memories-it will recover them. Pythagoras was right in the 'Golden Verses' when he upheld this view.

articles.title: Somnambulistic Telepathy - Lawyer N. Damaskinos
articles.excerpt: At age 15, Dimitrios N. Damaskinos saw in a half-sleep a thief stealing a case file; the theft was real, making this a classic case of somnambulistic telepathy.

content.value: The distinguished lawyer Dimitrios N. Damaskinos, at age 15 (1895), noted the following phenomenon published in the 1926 volume of Psychikai Ereynai.
His family home on Peiraios street had three floors: his bedroom and study below; his father's law office with staff and case boxes in the middle; and Supreme Court cases in the main office.

One June afternoon, resting because of the heat and half asleep, he saw this vision: he was in the main office when a blond man of medium height with a large mustache tiptoed in and approached the case boxes.

The stranger took a file from the 'Omega' slot labeled 'Vrailas v. Voulgaris.' Hastily he tore the edge of the folder, cut off the part with the parties' names, hid it in his pocket, and slipped away.
Waking in fright, young Damaskinos told his father, who thought him irrational. After insistence they checked the file and found one document missing: the copy of the appeal.

Police were notified; Damaskinos later recognized the culprit among suspects. He was a former process server of the office, dismissed for forgery and misconduct, who confessed he stole the file to sell it to the opposing side.
Damaskinos added that he then showed somnambulism due to mental overstrain, explaining his psychic sensitivity and reception of telepathic images.

Angelos Tanagras notes that sleepwalking and self-hypnosis are almost identical. Fatigue and half-sleep lowered the youth's conscious mind, letting him receive psychodynamic waves emitted by the thief, who obsessively thought about the act.
The episode is a characteristic case of somnambulistic telepathy, showing the marvelous capacities humans hide-suppressed by material existence but revealed in rare circumstances.

articles.title: Telepathy and Illusion - Case Studies
articles.excerpt: Dr. Levidis' double deathbed vision and other 1920s telepathy cases-representational, symbolic, and apparitional impressions of deaths and injuries.

content.value: The case of Dr Levidis, who interpreted the supposed apparition of the dead as telepathy.
Dr Mich. Levidis fell asleep at about half past one in the small hours of a night in May 1928, and woke roughly an hour later.
He then saw passing in front of his bed a little girl of three or four in a nightgown, who was, however, visible only as far as the waist.
The vision was so vivid that the doctor asked her: — What do you want here, my little one?
— I have died… she said, with the artlessness of her age. I am from the house next door…
With these words she was gone. Immediately afterwards, in her place, there appeared a young man of twenty-five dressed in black, who said: — I have just died too, but you do not know me!
And he too was gone.
The doctor, astonished by the visions, turned on the light, deliberately leaving it burning until morning as proof that he had not been dreaming.
At the same time he looked at the hour on his watch: it was 1.45 after midnight — about five or seven minutes to two, allowing for the watch running slightly slow.
When Levidis woke in the morning, he recounted the vision to his wife over breakfast.
Suddenly, as they were looking out of the window, they saw a mourning drape at the door next to theirs.
They were then informed that the sick, monomaniac little girl of their neighbour Grigorios Korialos had died — a child the doctor had never set eyes on.
The sequel to this event was reported to the “Society for Psychical Research”, and in person, by a relative of the little girl, Captain Spyr. Ferentinos.
Ferentinos confirmed that the death had occurred at exactly ten minutes to two in the morning, having looked at the hour on his own watch.
More interesting still is that, at the moment the funeral was arriving at the cemetery, his attention was caught by the lamentations of an old man who was following another coffin.
He asked who the dead man was, and was told that it was the young man of twenty-five, and that the mourner was his father.

The Levidis episode was announced by me at the session of the “Society for Psychical Research” on 4 April 1928, in the hall of the Archaeological Society, where Ferentinos was present among the audience.
The following day he came to the offices to ask for further information and to report his own observations as well.
At first impression, for those not versed in psychical phenomena, the episode gives the impression that the spirits of the dead did indeed appear in order to announce their deaths to Levidis.
The likelier explanation, however, is that this is simple telepathy, owing to the particular state Levidis was in, between sleep and waking, during which psychical phenomena become intense.

In this state Levidis was a sensitive telepathic receiver, and picked up, like a wireless signal, two psychic waves from two different directions — that is, from the places where the two deaths had occurred: that of the little girl and that of the young man of twenty-five.
The telepathy does not appear to have come directly from the deceased, but from persons present there at the moment of death, who communicated with Levidis.
As for the vision, the doctor’s brain, stirred by the impression, symbolised the drama through a hallucination taking the visual form of the dead.

The possibility that the spirits of the dead themselves were present is demolished by plain reasoning as well: these people would surely have had others dearer to them — their own households, for instance, who would have been grieving desperately — rather than appear to a stranger.
In parallel, in another case in 1928, the newspaper “Foni tou Laou” described a dream in which Aikaterini Prantouna saw great activity, agitation and priests in the house of a friend on Lefkada.
A few days later she was informed of the death of her nephew Michail.
In 1924 Aikaterini saw mourning on the balcony of Efthalia Kamara’s house, and a few hours later learned of Efthalia’s death — at precisely the hour of the vision.
In this case it is a matter of telepathy of the symbolic kind, in which her imagination symbolised the death by the customary black mourning of the balcony.
At that same period she saw in a dream that her fourteen-year-old son Miltiadis had cut off the finger of his right hand.
Two days later Miltiadis revealed to her that he had indeed cut the finger on that very day, but had been afraid to say so.
The wound had become infected and required an operation by Dr Nik. Orfanos.

This is telepathy of the representational kind, a phenomenon frequently observed, either according to the individual excitability of the brain or on account of circumstances in which the investigation is inadequate.

These small telepathic phenomena are of particular importance: they show how greatly varied the manifestations of thought-transference can be, and they help towards understanding the more complex phenomena, in which the imagination brings the dead into the account as well.
On 28 November 1928, Maria Milinariti (8 Monemvasias Street) saw, in a state of half-waking, an acquaintance of hers who was ill, Maria Karatza, aged twenty-five.
She was dressed all in white, and after greeting her with a bow, she vanished.
Milinariti got up at once and said to her daughter: — Niki, we must get ready quickly and go to Kallithea, to Maria’s house.
I am certain that she has died…
Indeed, when they reached Kallithea, they found the young woman dead.
Here too it is a matter of telepathy of the apparitional kind.

articles.title: A Promise to Appear After Death - Telepathy with Symbols
articles.excerpt: Chemist Spyridon Kokolis dreamt of his friend Fokion Negris visiting with an icy hand and a black ambulance-hours after Negris died-fulfilling a pact and illustrating symbolic telepathy.

content.value: The chemist Sp. Kokolis was talking one day with the late Fokion Negris about psychical phenomena, towards which Negris was hesitant, although he admitted their possibility.

Kokolis mentioned to him a recent incident, after which Negris said with a smile: “Well then, whichever of the two of us dies first, let him remember to present himself after death to the other, in order to convince him…”
Fifteen days before his death, Negris had given Kokolis a piece of ore for microscopic examination.
One night Kokolis saw in his sleep the maid announcing to him that Negris had come to visit him.

He received him, dreaming, and felt Negris’s hand cold as ice, while Negris refused to sit down and handed over the ore, saying: “I am in haste to depart… I have come to bid you farewell and to thank you. Keep this stone, and guard it! Farewell! I must go, for they are waiting for me… I am about to travel…”
Kokolis accompanied him as far as the door, where again he felt the iciness of his hand.
Instead of a motor car he saw a pitch-black first-aid vehicle, which vanished in a flash, as in the cinema.
When he woke, uneasy, he went to see whether Negris was ill, and learned from the newspaper that his friend had died the previous day at six in the evening.
The incident appears as the fulfilment of Negris’s promise, although for the psychophysiologist it constitutes an example of symbolic telepathy.
The telepathy took place later, when Kokolis found the right conditions of lowered consciousness to become a receiver.
The memory of the ore, given to him for examination, was mingled with the telepathic perception of the death, turning it into a keepsake.
Death is symbolised by the journey, by the frozen hand and by the black vehicle — symbols of the hearse.

A further symbolism of telepathy of the representational kind is cited in the case of the businessman Nik. Giannousopoulos, who saw in his sleep his friend dressed in radiant clothing together with an angel.
On that same day his friend became the father of a boy, while the angel symbolised the newborn child.
The Thessalian politician Alexandros Kassavetis reported three cases of symbolic dreams that foretold deaths.
These demonstrate the living symbolic role of the brain and its capacity to connect memories with events.
The succession of these dreams established that particular spatial presence as a symbol of death, which carried the telepathic message.
Symbolism and allegory play an important part in dreams and in the subconscious influence they exert.

articles.title: The Haunted House of Vythos, Kozani — Tanagras' Explanation of the Phenomena
articles.author: Angelos Tanagras
articles.excerpt: Angelos Tanagras explains the phenomena in the village of Vythos, Kozani. They have nothing to do with vampires or spirits, but are caused by human psychic radioactivity.

image.alt: The Haunted House of Vythos, Grammos

content.value: Mr. Tanagras explains the phenomena of Vythos.
They have nothing to do with vampires and spirits. They are caused by human radioactivity.
Mr. Angelos Tanagras, whom we approached to set out his view on the phenomena, sent us the following letter.
Dear Mr. Editor,

I am happy to respond to the request of 'Akropolis' for a scientific explanation of the phenomena in the village of Vythos in Grammos. I should inform you that these have nothing whatsoever to do with vampires, with spirits of the dead, or with so-called satanic forces.
In the present age, scientific research has clarified this matter with clarity, experimentally and definitively.

It has been observed that in certain inhabited houses, sometimes, due to intense emotional shocks experienced by the residents — especially after deaths, accidents, or painful illnesses — strange phenomena manifest that terrorise families and occasionally mobilise the police without result.

It is also natural that, in the event of a death among the residents, everyone should think the phenomena are a manifestation of the deceased's spirit. But since these phenomena consist of trivial acts such as moving objects, overturning furniture, knocks, or stone-throwing — which are easy to fabricate — their cause is not sought by investigators and the events remain unexplained, generally attributed to supernatural causes.

'If these phenomena originate from the deceased, would the spirits of the dead have no more serious manifestation than mere movements or at times childish acts such as — as occurred during the telekinetic phenomena of Messolonghi — moving boxes of Turkish delight and glasses full of water...'
One would be driven to despair over the value and intelligence of any future life.

Today, however, it has been proven experimentally and incontestably that these phenomena have an ENTIRELY DIFFERENT CAUSE and that they are produced unconsciously by THE LIVING INDIVIDUALS WHO INHABIT THE HOUSE and who have suffered a severe psychic shock.

It is indeed known that, besides radioactive substances (radium, uranium, etc.), many other substances can temporarily become radioactive — these are the so-called ISOTOPES that science uses in the treatment of various diseases.

Just as the inanimate primary substances of Chemistry can do so, in a similar way living beings — humans — can, through the influence of powerful psychic shocks, emit A KIND OF PSYCHIC RADIOACTIVITY, which is the cause of the phenomena that people in all latitudes call 'HAUNTED HOUSE PHENOMENA.'

The remarkable thing is that this psychoradiant emission is activated CONSCIOUSLY WITH SUPERHUMAN PROPERTIES, even with dynamic properties such as the movement of objects. This experimental finding IS OF THE GREATEST SIGNIFICANCE, because through it the existence of the SOUL within the LIVING BODY is proven.

Similar misunderstood phenomena, a century ago in America, were considered undeniable proof of communication with the dead and were the cause of the formulation of the SPIRITUALIST THEORY and the spread of spiritualism with its 'little tables' and alphabetic boards.

In the volumes of my 'Psychical Researches' (1925–1932), which ceased publication after the Occupation, a multitude of similar phenomena in Greece have been recorded during the 29 years of activity of the Society for Psychical Research — whose work failed to arouse the interest of the official intellectual institutions of the country.
In our Greece, similar research will be established when it has been naturalised as far as Azerbaijan.

So, in the phenomena of the village of Vythos too, certainly one of the four women living in the house — either the mother or one of the daughters — having suffered psychic shock as a result of the grandmother's death, is the unconscious cause of the phenomena, and the good people of the village have been needlessly terrified.
The kindly old woman who now rests in peace in the village cemetery is entirely innocent of what has occurred.

Moreover, the reporter from 'Akropolis' observed on the spot the girls' abnormal nervousness. Above all, the information that their mother is 45 years old — that is, in the MENOPAUSAL PERIOD of women's lives, during which, due to the cessation of ovarian function and menstruation, the hormonal balance is disturbed...

And the remedy in such social disturbances, where superstition may lead to great excesses, is THE IDENTIFICATION OF THE PSYCHOKINETIC MEMBER OF THE FAMILY — THE CAUSE OF THE PHENOMENA — AND THEIR IMMEDIATE REMOVAL.

The measures I have always recommended to local police authorities and local scientists in cases of psychokinetic manifestations are TO REMOVE, ONE BY ONE AND SUCCESSIVELY, FOR AS MANY DAYS AS NEEDED, the members of the family to nearby villages, until it is established, following the removal of the individual...
Fortunately, however, psychokinetic manifestations DO NOT LAST long. They cease as soon as the nervous system calms and the psychic shock is alleviated.

I am certain that the local police authorities of the Gendarmerie and City Police — those who attended my lectures, which I am invited to give at special police academies — will provide a reassuring scientific explanation of these phenomena.
Angelos Tanagras

articles.title: The Servant — Telekinetic Medium of Thasos, 1938
articles.author: Petros Angelopoulos
articles.excerpt: Angelos Tanagras in Thasos attributes the mysterious telekinetic phenomena to the young servant Sevasti, whom he described as an exceptional medium.

image.alt: The servant — telekinetic medium of Thasos

content.value: The Mysterious Phenomena of Thasos
How the phenomena unfolded — The President of the Society for Psychical Research attributes them to the young servant — An exceptional Medium — He will bring her to Athens.

Mr. Tanagras is in Thasos, where he is examining strange and mysterious telekinetic phenomena that have been occurring for two months on the beautiful island and have thrown its residents into turmoil. The director of the Society for Psychical Research was in fact summoned by the residents themselves to investigate the phenomena.
The case is as follows:

About two months ago, mysterious stone-throwing began at the house of Mr. Giannakis at the harbour of Thasos. The stones fell only on the roof of Mr. Giannakis' house, mainly at midnight. At that hour, knocks were heard and stones fell, and this phenomenon lasted only a few minutes.

From that point on, there was no other topic of conversation but the stone-throwing at the Giannakis house and other mysterious telekinetic phenomena. Many stories circulated among the residents of Thasos — many true and many imaginary — but in all of them the same name kept appearing. The name Sevasti belonged to...

The police, in view of these rumours and the general unrest among the residents, referred Mr. Giannakis to the misdemeanours court, which sentenced him, his wife, and Sevasti to 25 days in prison for disturbing the peace.

But even after the conviction, the telekinetic phenomena continued, along with the rumours among the residents, some of whom wrote a letter to Mr. Tanagras in which, after recounting the events, they begged him to come to Thasos to investigate.

Mr. Tanagras, upon receiving that letter, set off for Thasos and arrived on 15 March 1938. At the island's shore, many residents greeted him with enthusiasm and all began at once to recount the events to him.

Upon his arrival, he went to the Giannakis house where he visited the servant Sevasti. Her whole appearance — the pallor of her face, the sensitivity of her nerves, the weakness of her body — proved that her organism was not functioning normally. To Mr. Tanagras' initial questions she answered vaguely.

He then inspected the chicken coop, on whose roof were gathered the stones that had fallen mysteriously for 20 consecutive nights at midnight. When Mr. Tanagras saw the heap, his brow furrowed. He then entered the Giannakis house, where all the fragile objects lay broken — shattered while Sevasti had been nearby.

Mr. Tanagras, in the room where he found himself together with others, summoned Sevasti and ordered her to knock down a shoehorn hanging on the wall. Sevasti obeyed the command and the moment she looked at the shoehorn, it fell to the floor without her touching it. Those present made the sign of the cross; Sevasti stood half-dazed and motionless.

Mr. Tanagras then presented her with a trap containing 4 small mice and released them at a distance of two metres from where the servant was sitting. The little mice, as if hypnotised, made their way towards her and came to a stop at her feet. Those watching made the sign of the cross once more...
Mr. Tanagras then halted the experiments, fearing that Sevasti's constitution might become exhausted.

These two experiments became known among the people of Thasos and caused some to experience an irresistible urge to laugh and others astonishment and the urge to cross themselves. Among the latter, many said that Sevasti had in the past been the cause of many disasters. Once she entered a grocer's shop and boxes began to fall...

Mr. Tanagras will continue his experiments, remaining in Thasos for another 3 days. Regarding Sevasti, he said that the phenomena are attributable to her on account of the specific functioning of her constitution, since she is in her 19th year and shows abnormalities in the manifestation of normal physiological phenomena...
Sevasti in Athens

The President of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr. Tanagras, has returned from Thasos and in a statement emphasised that the medium Sevasti is extraordinary. Mr. Tanagras declared that he will bring her to Athens and keep her at his home in order to monitor her psychical phenomena.

articles.title: The Rouf Phenomena - 1929
articles.excerpt: Mysterious psychic incidents in the Rouf district caused panic; Angelos Tanagras explained them as hysteria, suggestion, and mass mimicry.

content.value: How the strange and mysterious phenomena that have thrown Rouf into uproar are to be explained

The various rumours of mysterious phenomena — young Christodoulou and M. Papadimitriou suffered hysterical aphonia — yesterday both were in perfect health — They refuse to be photographed but consented to be sketched — Is a love affair being concealed?
In the Rouf quarter, strange psychical phenomena manifested themselves in the case of young Christos Christodoulou and of Maritsa Papadimitriou. The quarter continues to be in uproar.

Yesterday strange rumours began to circulate among the inhabitants of Rouf: that other people too, small boys and girls, had suffered epileptic fits, that they had been struck with aphasia and had begun to converse with invisible powers, at the sight of which they reacted sometimes with cries and sometimes by fainting.

Particular mention is made of a “street child” of the Rouf quarter, who lives on alms and on the small payments he receives for various errands he runs, since he is entirely without protection and has neither parents nor relatives.

Concerning this boy, rumours circulated yesterday that he had seen in his sleep the icon of the Panagia, and that it lies buried in some alley of the quarter; whereupon many devout people who believed the dream began digging at various points in the district to find the icon. It goes without saying that all their labour was in vain, for the icon was not found.
What happened to our photographer

The day before yesterday, when, on the first rumours of strange phenomena in the Rouf quarter, editors of the “Akropolis” were sent to establish what had occurred and to photograph young Christos and the girl to whom the aphasia had been transmitted, a curious thing happened to our newspaper’s photographer, as we wrote yesterday.

Young Christos and Maritsa would on no account be photographed, claiming that when the Panagia had revealed herself to Christos she had forbidden him to… pose before a camera lens, for reasons unknown.

The two patients reacted so wildly at the sight of the camera that the photographer was obliged to leave the house in which they were staying, in order that the hysterical youth should stop gesticulating and shouting. But the moment the photographer, now at a great distance from the house, tried to photograph its exterior, young Christodoulou — who was inside the house and had no line of sight to the outside, the doors and windows being shut — began once again to shout violently, the instant the photograph was taken.

Yesterday, by contrast, the boy was in excellent spirits, for his crisis had passed, and he consented to pose to be sketched; indeed he declared that he wanted the sketch to be a fine one, and when he saw it he was entirely satisfied. Maritsa, who was likewise in good condition, also wanted to be sketched, but her parents would not allow it.
The two young people’s day yesterday

Since the evening before last the two young people have come through the great tempest that had thrown the whole quarter into uproar. They were very calm and in good spirits, and explained to the curious passers-by who came to learn more what had happened, what they had seen and what they had felt at the time of their crisis. They remember it all down to the last detail and recount it without end.

Maritsa is always sparing of words; she keeps silent and is content to let Christos speak on behalf of them both. This handsome adolescent never stops relating the same things — by now familiar to all readers of the “Akropolis” — to whoever asks him.
When our colleagues visited him yesterday, they found him reading the newspaper and confirming what had been written.
He still remembers what he said, how his family behaved towards him, what each of them was doing at the time of his crisis — everything, with wonderful precision.
I did not want to kill myself

Among other things, he did not omit to tell our editors that he had not wanted to kill himself when he made those incomprehensible movements and beat himself, but that he had simply wanted to tear out his own eyes.
— Because I did not know either, he says, but I felt a force compelling me to tear out my eyes, and that force I truly could not resist, although I understood that this was my ruin.

As he was saying this, we pointed out to him that his right eye is a little scratched at the side, and that he bears other abrasions on various parts of his face, which show the truth of what he says. At the same time Christos affirms that he did indeed see the Panagia, and that he beat his head against the wall without knowing why.
What Mr Tanagras says

In order to have a scientific explanation of this curious phenomenon of the Rouf quarter, we visited Mr Angelos Tanagras as the most competent authority, and asked his opinion. As was reported in yesterday’s evening papers, Mr Tanagras, at the request of the City Police, visited the two young psychopaths at their home, and they were taken by car to the offices of the Society for Psychical Research so that he might examine them in detail.

Mr Tanagras gave it as his opinion that this is an ordinary phenomenon of hysterical aphonia and that it encloses no mystery whatever, while its transmission to Maritsa is due to autosuggestion, on account of the intense emotion the young woman felt when she saw the condition of young Christos, with whom, as it appears, she is closely connected.
At the bottom of all this it is not out of the question that some earlier love affair lies hidden, which allowed the state of transmission by autosuggestion of the phenomenon to operate.
Mr Tanagras told us, among other things, that it is possible for this condition to be transmitted to still more people, and that this ought to surprise nobody.
Chorea and mimicry

It is possible, he told us, for many people, through autosuggestion, either to suffer aphasia or to have transmitted to them that nervous condition of “chorea”, as it is called in the language of the psychical sciences, which is characterised by violent, abrupt movements and jerkings of the various limbs of the body — arms, legs, head and so on — and is due to an irritation of the nerves. This condition is transmitted to two or three, or even to many more people; and on account of the irregular violent movements, which resemble the movements of an infant, the phenomenon was given the name “chorea”.

The transmission of the movements from one person to another, through suggestion, takes place even without the person to whom the movement is transmitted willing it at all. It rests upon a great law of nature, that of “mimicry” — that is, the tendency existing in matter (organic or inorganic, dead or living) to want to repeat phenomena that have occurred once, or to imitate automatically what is taking place in its immediate surroundings.

As for young Christodoulou and his claim that he saw a vision of the Panagia, Mr Tanagras told us that he will indeed have seen this vision, because he is under the influence of religious traditions, an influence which impressed upon his mind that the appearances of imaginary persons, saints and so forth are possible.

Mr Tanagras also offered his congratulations on the well-judged action of the City Police, who notified the Society for Psychical Research so that it might examine the events scientifically and give the true explanation.

articles.title: Telekinetic Phenomena in an Abandoned House at Makrisia, Ilia - 1933
articles.excerpt: In Makrisia, Ilia, an empty house is shaken by bangs and flying furniture; terrified villagers keep vigil while two young men try to confront the 'demons.'

content.value: Do demons dance in Makrisia of Olympia?
The deserted house where furniture dances - villagers panic - the daring of two youths who do not believe.

New turmoil in Makrisia. Telekinetic phenomena that shook the village three months ago returned even stronger. Just as residents thought the 'evil spirits' had left, new bangs, vague voices, and the sound of furniture overturning from the Gkotsis house in the center of town alarmed them again.
Terrified, people rushed out and gathered at a distance around the haunted house, unwilling to approach for fear of a repeat of the earlier comic-tragic episode born of rustic naivety.
Two young men determined to find the source spent several midnights armed with knives, revolvers, and flashlights on the second floor, where they thought the demons danced.
Revolvers in the left hand-tradition says only a left-handed shot kills a demon-they awaited the intruders.
At midnight their pulse hit 150. In the half-light, furniture turned in their anxious imagination into threatening black masses with tails and horns and blazing eyes.
Soon a fierce wind of unknown origin swept the room; furniture rose and crashed to the floor, while cries echoed from unseen places.

They swept their flashlights everywhere seeking the invisible hands, fingers of their left hands on the triggers. Seeing nothing, thinking pranksters caused the noise, they stayed frozen until the racket stopped.

Meanwhile villagers watching from outside prepared to return home when they saw, with unspeakable terror, the front door open and two shadowy figures emerge holding revolvers and spewing fire from their mouths (they held lanterns).
They thought demons had emerged to chase them and fled en masse, fearing to lose their speech. The two youths struggled to explain it was only them.

Thus the same events of 5-6 February repeated; once more the villagers lost their peace. According to later reports the tension remains; many spend nights outdoors listening in dread to midnight noises and howls.
They urgently requested Tanagras' arrival to identify the psychic force causing the telekinesis and end phenomena the villagers attribute to vampires.

Tanagras' visit is deemed necessary to fully clarify the matter. Similar telekinesis occurred five years earlier in Messolonghi, where cafe furniture danced at midday due to a waiter named Rapanakia with such powers.

articles.title: Mysterious Stone-Throwing and Falling Objects in Tambouria Continue - 1932
articles.excerpt: Angelos Tanagras visits Tambouria where stones, coins, and objects rain nightly; a 13-year-old girl is suspected as the medium behind the telekinesis.

content.value: A night visit from Mr Tanagras — a rain… of ten-lepta pieces and drachmas — These are telekinetic phenomena — the part played by a thirteen-year-old girl.

The President of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr Angelos Tanagras, seems as though he will never find any peace. Strange phenomena that may possibly bear upon the psychical sciences are observed at Lamia, in Evia, at Messolonghi, at Thessaloniki. Mr Tanagras is everywhere. Could he then have escaped the sensational telekinetic phenomena of the Tampouria quarter? Quite impossible. The Society’s telephone was all but breaking.
Mr Tanagras, for God’s sake, take pity on us, the stones are falling like rain!

The whole quarter had learned of Mr Tanagras’s coming, and so, when the car that brought him reached the boundary of Piraeus and Tampouria, Mr Tanagras was met by hundreds of people, whom a very strong police force under a sub-inspector could scarcely hold back. All the streets leading to the mysterious house at 134 Goura Street were packed with people. Outside the house of Mr M. Apostolopoulos a second cordon of constables had been formed. Mr Tanagras’s arrival was greeted with sighs of relief.
At last the mystery which had exercised them for so long — nearly two months — was to be solved.

The task of briefing Mr Tanagras on the mystery was undertaken by a charming young lady, the head of the Piraeus branch of the electricity company, who herself takes a lofty interest in psychophysiology: Miss Galateia Chamodraka.

The phenomena began two months ago. One evening, as Mrs Apostolopoulou was sitting in her yard, she was struck by a stone. Since then, every evening, the stones fall like rain. And it is not only stones that fall, but anything you can imagine.

One of the numerous victims of the phenomena, Mr Othon Raftopoulos, undertook to bring in the mysterious “output” of the last few days. And what was it? A basket full of things of every kind. Stones, screws, pocket-knives, pencils, roof tiles, broken plates and whatever else you please. And something which shows that the spirit attends to its hair: a matchbox with a tube of brilliantine tucked inside it.
Very suspicious things, said Mr Tanagras, laughing.
Miss Chamodraka was puzzled: How odd. On other nights at this hour, half past nine, the stones were falling in torrents.

She had not finished her sentence when a frightened young man came up and reported to Mr Tanagras: This very moment I was speaking with the policeman, and then, without understanding how, I was struck by a stone. It seemed to me that it fell straight down.
Was it warm? asks Mr Tanagras. No, cold! answers the young man. Then it is not a phenomenon.
And Mr Tanagras explains: The stones that fall in cases of telekinetic phenomena are, as a rule, warm.
Ten-lepta pieces, twenty-lepta pieces and francs.
Shall we not go out into the yard? suggests Miss Chamodraka. Perhaps the phenomena will be brought on.

She was not at all wrong. We had scarcely sat down in the yard when the phenomena began from its vine arbour. The first to receive them was a colleague (a journalist of the Akropolis). While we were talking he cried out:
— Something has fallen on me!
A metallic sound followed. We bent down to see the “miracle”. A little twenty-lepta piece!

We had no time to recover, and the phenomena continued in rich production. Ten-lepta pieces, twenty-lepta pieces, five-lepta pieces and drachmas came falling… mysteriously from the arbour. The work of gathering them up began, and shortly afterwards came the balance sheet: — 16.80. Three packets of cigarettes, was the answer.
Mr Tanagras had the floor: Mr President, do you say these are really telekinetic phenomena? Perhaps they would be real if what fell were… pounds sterling, answered Mr Tanagras, laughing.

The phenomena had no intention of stopping. A lady, at the very moment when Mr Tanagras was speaking, was struck by a stone. She bent down at once to pick it up. “Warm! Warm!” she cried. Mr Tanagras took hold of it too: “Cold, quite cold,” he answered her.
The mystery had no intention of being solved. The small change and the stone that had fallen were of no significance whatever.
— Let us try to find the medium, said Mr Tanagras.

And we all moved into the parlour of the Apostolopoulos family. Mr Tanagras took charge of the examination. He took a compass out of his pocket and called the inhabitants one by one to sit their… examinations. They stretched out their hands and tried, with the movements Mr Tanagras indicated to them, to move the compass. Nothing. The compass had no intention of moving at all.
In this way they were all examined. Only one little girl was missing, about fourteen years old — that is to say, at the age of puberty. Ritsa Raftopoulou.
Perhaps the little one is the medium, said Mr Tanagras. At the age of puberty, both men and women produce phenomena of telekinesis.
Her examination began. The compass moved faintly.

The examination must continue, said Mr Tanagras with interest. The examination did indeed continue, but within a narrow family circle. Mr Tanagras, little Ritsa and her brother Mr Othon Raftopoulos withdrew to their rooms. We remained behind. The minutes seemed to us like centuries.
Will the mystery be solved at last? The door of the room of the… holy inquisition opens hurriedly. The little girl comes out frightened.
What is the matter, Ritsa? I am afraid! They closed my eyes, they kept telling me to sleep. The moment I was about to fall asleep I took fright. What was that?
Mr Tanagras comes out.

Has it been found, Mr President? Perhaps; it is by no means improbable that it is a matter of the little girl. She is of a nervous constitution, and that contributes. The mystery, however, cannot be solved at once, and Mr Tanagras gives instructions.
Take the little girl away from the house for a few days. Then, if she is the medium, the phenomena will stop.

Our mission ended here. Not so that of the police, however. For up to yesterday fifteen practical jokers had been arrested and convicted who, taking advantage of the phenomena, had literally wrecked Mr Apostolopoulos’s house with stones.
As we were parting from Mr Tanagras, he said to us: If the little one could have been hypnotised, the mystery would have been solved tonight. But mysteries are not easily solved.

articles.title: Telekinetic Phenomena at Kalamaki - 1937
articles.author: Akropolis
articles.excerpt: Clothing slashed and objects disturbed in merchant Drakopoulos' Kalamaki home in 1937, traced to the unconscious telekinesis of his 16-year-old servant.

image.alt: Telekinetic phenomena in a Kalamaki home (1937)

content.value: New telekinetic phenomena have come to light in recent days at Kalamaki, in the house of the Stadiou Street merchant Mr Drakopoulos.

These phenomena manifested themselves a few days ago and present an astonishing resemblance to those which had appeared two years previously in the house of General Mr Diamantopoulos, over which a great deal of noise had been made, and are due, like those, to the young maid of the house.

Thus, a few days ago, when the phenomena first manifested themselves in Mr Drakopoulos’s house, it was observed that various garments and items of furnishing and clothing belonging to the family were being damaged without cause.

At first it was supposed that the damage was due to the carelessness of the young maid or of some other person in the house; but when it was established that it was continuing, while various precautionary measures were being taken, the household grew anxious and expressed their anxieties to friends.
The damage was done chiefly to fabrics, which appeared to have been cut with scissors.

The holes formed in the fabrics and the garments had, as in the case of the telekinetic experiments at General Mr Diamantopoulos’s house, an entirely regular shape, as though they had been made by a particular person with a pair of scissors — a fact which pointed to conscious action.
THEY ARE DUE TO THE MAID

The Drakopoulos family, as soon as they observed that the phenomena were being repeated, hastened to notify the Kalamaki police, and also applied to the Society for Psychical Research for the solution of the mystery.
The president of the Society, Mr Angelos Tanagras, according to our information, visited the house where the phenomena were being observed and solved the mystery.

He gave it as his opinion, that is, that these are ordinary telekinetic phenomena produced unconsciously by the young sixteen-year-old maid of the house, Anna Apergi, who had been in service at Mr Drakopoulos’s house for some months.
On Mr Tanagras’s recommendation, the young maid was removed from the house, and it is certain that the phenomena will cease entirely and that calm will be restored to the household.
WHAT MR TANAGRAS SAYS
Mr Tanagras, whom one of our editors met, made the following statement concerning the Kalamaki phenomena:
“The phenomena are undoubtedly due to Mr Drakopoulos’s young maid, who is at the age of adolescence.
There are persons who, under the influence of puberty or of other organic upheavals, become dynamolytic, like radioactive bodies.
Instead of this energy manifesting itself as illness or as an hysterical fit, it finds an outlet in dynamolysis, which constitutes the cause of the so-called haunted houses.
The phenomena always accompany one particular person of the household; when that person is removed, they cease, or else manifest themselves in a new place.
The phenomena also correspond to the hidden and unavowed feelings of the dynamolytic person, such as resentment and psychic tension.
That is why destruction is caused to clothing, furniture and objects.
The same occurred in the case of General Diamantopoulos, where damage of some 25,000 drachmas was caused.
In the Drakopoulos case the phenomenon was clearer still, since his own belongings were left untouched, while the lady’s dresses and the household linen suffered damage.
Mr Tanagras also mentioned cases of psychobolia, which the common people attribute to the evil eye, explaining that all of these have the same radioactive cause as the telekinetic phenomena.
