content.value: Angelos Goulandris — The young man of Athens who converses with the dead — 1936
Scientific circles were left astonished, not knowing to what to attribute this extraordinary phenomenon
AND YET IT IS NO HOAX

ATHENS, 12th, by air. — On a corner of Ioannou Moreos Street, a very short distance from the Veikou stop, and in a single-storey detached house, things are happening that have thrown the whole Gargaretta district into uproar.

At house number B on Ioannou Moreos Street lives the Goulandris family, originally from Constantinople, made up of the couple and two male children. The elder of these, sixteen years of age, is called Angelos and attends — or rather attended until recently — the Leonteios Lyceum. Since last winter, however, young Angelos has been seized by some mysterious illness, in consequence of which he broke off his studies.

He imagined, that is, two or three times a week and at a particular hour — specifically between eleven and twelve at night — that some historical personage was becoming incarnate within him, who obliged him to shut himself alone in a room of the said house, where he would receive the written instructions and commands of this personage, who sat before him in the flesh and luminous.

The boy, under the influence of an indescribable nervous over-excitement, would listen to the materialised spirit and write down its instructions. He has since filled whole pages with such opinions and directions. This was happening, and happens to this day, two or three times a week. The boy’s parents, growing anxious, kept the matter secret from everyone and called in the university lecturer, the pathologist Mr Petzetakis, to examine their son.

In the meantime, however, the affair became known throughout the district on account of the tremendous crashes that accompanied every arrival and departure of the spirit, and the neighbours concluded that the house was haunted. At the hour of the communication they gather in groups outside the house to follow the noises that are heard.
WHAT MR PETZETAKIS SAYS
The lecturer who examined the boy explains the affair as follows:
I was indeed called in recently to examine this young man medically.

He is a person of good health and excellent mental condition, so long as he is examined in a sober state. At certain moments, however, he presents disturbances of the neurophysical system. That is, he is suddenly seized by muscular spasms, particularly in the muscles of the arm, and then he goes in violently, as if driven by an irresistible force, and rapidly shuts himself in a room of his house, where he sits on a chair in front of a table.
This is accompanied by demonic crashes, as well as by movements of objects, which are transmitted throughout the whole house.

The young man relates that he sees a luminescence issuing from his head, which luminescence within a short time turns into an historical personage. Then the crashes cease and a conversation begins between him and the said personage, which is heard perfectly distinctly by third parties. The voice is deep and of lesser volume than the young man’s own. When the conversation is over the crashes return, the young man comes out of the room and recounts in detail everything that was said.
Examination of the youth immediately after the end of the conversation — which lasts an hour and a half — finds him entirely sound mentally, as though nothing had happened.
Organically, he presents tachycardia of a high degree, which lasts for half an hour after the end of the conversation.

Following this phenomenon we wished to examine the matter more scientifically as well, proposing the placing of a microphone in the room, and the photographing of the luminous arc which precedes — by the boy’s own account — the luminous form of the historical personage; but his family persistently refused.
In my opinion, these are ordinary telekinetic phenomena.

What is scientifically interesting here is the question of the second voice. For we do not know whether this is unconscious ventriloquism, appearing at the moment of the trance in which the boy finds himself, or whether it is an ectoplasmic voice — a thing it would be scientifically interesting to establish.
THE EXPLANATION OF THE PHENOMENA
Mr Petzetakis, asked by a journalist how the phenomena of Gargaretta are to be explained scientifically, stated the following:

The phenomena produced by young Angelos Goulandris are among the ordinary telekinetic phenomena, which manifest themselves particularly at the age of adolescence in persons of a hysterical nature. These either disappear abruptly or last for a considerable time, developing into various forms.

The psychical phenomena of young Goulandris present themselves in the form of vision, telekinesis, automatism and ectoplasmic action. The ectoplasmic action develops at a given moment of trance in the person by whom the phenomena are produced. It acts without his will and outside his body, in various ways.
To the ectoplasmic force no explanation can be given by science.

On these phenomena I am collaborating with the president of the Society for Psychical Research, Mr Tanagras, who likewise gave it as his opinion that these are ordinary telekinetic phenomena, which appear in certain persons at the age of adolescence.
AND THE SOVEREIGN PEOPLE

The lecturer Mr Petzetakis, for his part, recounted the history, collaborated with Mr Tanagras, mustered the fitting terminology, and then, having gone on to explain the phenomenon of ectoplasmic force, replied that science can give no explanation whatever.
The history, then, and the terms enlightened us in no respect at all. We came away uninformed, poor in judgements and impressions, without any exact knowledge or explanation of the phenomenon.
There remained only the house, the crashes, the phenomena. So we arrived at Veikou, went on, and had no need to search for the house.

Dense masses of people revealed it to us. The whole population of the district had ringed it about. And they were heads of families returning to their homes, young working men and girls scraping a living, housewives in their slippers, their dressing gowns and with their babies.
The servant girls of the district, the people living round about, and the “whitebait”. Whitebait by the dozen and by the hundred, from five to ten, to twelve, to fifteen years of age.

A policeman, a cool spectator of the affair, when the journalist asked what was going on, replied with assurance:

- It is nothing. A television.
And he continued on his round.
And the people? They were most talkative. Informed? Most critical.
Most of them had heard the crashes. Others heard whistling, others saw a flash, and every one of them had heard something and seen something.

- But what is it the boy sees, ladies?
- Why, haven’t you heard?
- No.
- He sees some politician, and the man dictates screeds to him three times a week and instructs him to deliver them years later, when the boy comes of age.

And the baker from across the way, completing the bulletin of information, added:

- Tomorrow, though, he will not be coming alone, but in company with somebody else.

And the discussions go on in this tone; the comments and the expressions of popular disbelief, or of the credulity of the crowd, break out now in one group, now in another, and arguments arise, contradictions and differences of opinion are voiced, ironies are uttered and light skirmishes take place.

They are all of them well-known judges, however — competent authorities, oracles. For all that, nobody becomes any the wiser, not even from this many-mouthed popular exegesis. And nothing remains but to follow the matter ourselves and interpret it.
I APOGEVMATINI, 12.09.1936, p. 1
